story_description: Extend HookRunner to accept provider and worktree parameters, enabling hooks to execute differently based on which CLI (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI) triggered them and which worktree context applies
task_description: Modify HookRunner.executeHooks() to accept provider and worktreeId parameters, route events through provider-specific filtering, and pass provider context to hook execution environment
atom_description: Add provider:HookProvider and worktreeId:UUID? parameters to executeHooks() function, implement provider filtering logic, update hook execution context to include provider metadata, and ensure backwards compatibility with existing hook configurations
problem_statement: Currently HookRunner.executeHooks() executes hooks without knowing which CLI provider triggered the event, making it impossible to run provider-specific hooks or pass provider context to hook scripts. This blocks multi-CLI support where hooks need different behavior for Claude Code vs Gemini CLI vs Codex CLI.
scope_in: Modify executeHooks() signature to add provider:HookProvider and worktreeId:UUID? parameters
Add provider filtering logic to skip hooks not matching current provider
Update HookExecutionContext to include provider and worktreeId metadata
Set BLAZE_HOOK_PROVIDER and BLAZE_WORKTREE_ID environment variables for hook scripts
Maintain backwards compatibility with existing hook configurations that lack provider field
Add unit tests for provider filtering and context passing
scope_out: Provider detection from session context (handled by H009-CONTEXT)
UI for selecting providers (handled by H005-UIPROVIDER)
Hook migration between providers (handled by H007-MIGRATE)
Event name mapping between providers (handled by H001-TYPES)
assumptions: HookProvider enum already exists from H001-TYPES atom
HookConfiguration model already supports optional provider field from H002-CONFIG atom
Existing hooks without provider field should execute for all providers (backwards compatibility)
Hook scripts can read environment variables for provider context
UUID type is available from Foundation framework
Worktree IDs follow UUID format and are optional (nil for non-worktree sessions)
constraints: Must not break existing hook configurations that lack provider field
Must maintain async/await execution model for hook running
Environment variable names must use BLAZE_ prefix for namespacing
Provider filtering must happen before hook execution to avoid unnecessary process spawning
Must handle nil worktreeId gracefully for sessions without worktree context
Hook execution timeout (30s default) must remain unchanged
functional_requirements: FR1: executeHooks() accepts provider:HookProvider parameter specifying which CLI triggered the event
FR2: executeHooks() accepts optional worktreeId:UUID? parameter for worktree-scoped hooks
FR3: Hooks with matching provider field execute for that provider only
FR4: Hooks with nil/missing provider field execute for all providers (wildcard behavior)
FR5: HookExecutionContext.provider property exposes current provider to hook logic
FR6: HookExecutionContext.worktreeId property exposes optional worktree context
FR7: Hook scripts receive BLAZE_HOOK_PROVIDER environment variable with provider rawValue
FR8: Hook scripts receive BLAZE_WORKTREE_ID environment variable when worktreeId is non-nil
FR9: HookExecutionResult includes provider that triggered the hook for logging/debugging
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Provider filtering adds less than 1ms overhead per hook evaluation
NFR2: Memory allocation for environment variables remains under 1KB per hook execution
NFR3: Backwards compatibility verified with existing Claude Code hooks
NFR4: Thread-safe execution suitable for concurrent hook running
implementation_steps: Step 1: Update executeHooks() function signature to add provider:HookProvider and worktreeId:UUID? parameters with default value nil for worktreeId
Step 2: Add provider:HookProvider and worktreeId:UUID? properties to HookExecutionContext struct
Step 3: Implement filterHooks(for:provider) helper that returns hooks matching provider or having nil provider field
Step 4: Insert filterHooks call at start of executeHooks() to reduce hook list before iteration
Step 5: Update buildEnvironment() to add BLAZE_HOOK_PROVIDER=provider.rawValue entry
Step 6: Update buildEnvironment() to conditionally add BLAZE_WORKTREE_ID=worktreeId.uuidString when non-nil
Step 7: Update HookExecutionResult to include triggeredBy:HookProvider property
Step 8: Update all existing executeHooks() call sites to pass provider parameter
Step 9: Add filterHooks unit tests verifying wildcard and specific provider matching
Step 10: Add environment variable injection unit tests verifying BLAZE_HOOK_PROVIDER and BLAZE_WORKTREE_ID
Step 11: Add integration test running real hook script that echoes provider environment variable
api_contracts: executeHooks(for:provider:worktreeId:) -> [HookExecutionResult]: Main entry point for hook execution with provider context
filterHooks(for:provider:) -> [HookConfiguration]: Internal helper returning hooks that match provider or have nil provider
buildEnvironment(context:) -> [String:String]: Returns environment dictionary including BLAZE_HOOK_PROVIDER and optional BLAZE_WORKTREE_ID
event_contracts: HookExecutionStarted: Includes provider field for observability
HookExecutionCompleted: Includes provider field and worktreeId if present
HookExecutionFailed: Includes provider field for debugging provider-specific failures
edge_cases: EC1: Hook configuration has provider field set to unknown string - treat as non-matching, log warning
EC2: worktreeId is nil but hook script expects BLAZE_WORKTREE_ID - environment variable simply not set
EC3: All hooks filtered out for provider - return empty array, no error
EC4: Provider enum gains new case after hooks created - existing hooks continue matching by wildcard
EC5: Hook timeout occurs during provider-aware execution - result includes provider for debugging
EC6: Concurrent executeHooks calls with different providers - each maintains isolated provider context
failure_modes: FM1: Invalid provider value in configuration JSON - Skip hook with warning log, continue execution
FM2: Environment variable injection fails - Log error, execute hook without provider context
FM3: Hook script crashes when reading BLAZE_HOOK_PROVIDER - Captured in HookExecutionResult.error
FM4: Memory pressure from many concurrent provider-aware hooks - Existing semaphore limits apply
rollback_plan: Revert to previous executeHooks() signature without provider/worktreeId parameters. Remove HookExecutionContext.provider and .worktreeId properties. Remove environment variable injection. Existing hooks continue working as they did before.

open_questions: Should worktreeId default to nil or require explicit passing at all call sites?
Should we log all filtered-out hooks at DEBUG level or only on verbose flag?
Should HookExecutionResult.triggeredBy be optional to support legacy results?
notes: This atom is foundational for multi-CLI hook support. The provider filtering logic must be efficient since it runs on every hook execution. Backwards compatibility is critical - existing users should notice no behavior change unless they explicitly add provider fields to their hooks.

risks: Breaking change if existing code passes wrong number of arguments to executeHooks()
Performance regression if provider filtering is inefficient with large hook sets
Environment variable naming collision with user-defined variables
Race condition if provider context not properly isolated in concurrent execution
mitigations: Add provider parameter with no default to force compile-time errors at all call sites, ensuring explicit updates
Implement filterHooks as O(n) single-pass filter, benchmark with 100+ hooks to verify under 10ms
Use BLAZE_ prefix namespace to minimize collision risk, document reserved prefix
Store provider in HookExecutionContext struct passed by value, ensuring isolation
risk_register.blast_radius: Limited to hook execution path. Does not affect session management, UI rendering, or data persistence. Failed hooks already have error handling and do not crash the app.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If provider filtering causes issues, add feature flag BLAZE_DISABLE_PROVIDER_FILTERING=1 that bypasses filter and executes all hooks regardless of provider field. This maintains existing behavior while investigation continues.
